name: twisted-planter
why: The part the web playground opens first, so it has to build, and read right, on a stranger's first visit. Two bodies. The planter: a ruled star loft twisted 60° through nine sections, cut hollow by the same star inset 3 mm at the same section heights, with seven drains through a flat base of 12·½·34·26.52·sin 30° − 7·π·2.5² = 2567.6 mm² (read 2567.96). The saucer: one revolved section with rounded corners plus six 30 × 2 × 3 mm radial ridges, exactly 1080 mm³ more than the section alone, set between the drains so the planter stands 3 mm clear of the saucer floor and water can leave; between_bodies reads the two touching on the ridges and nowhere else. measure_wall_thickness reads the wall at 2.0 mm with the rim edge rounded; on the sharp rim it reports hundredths of a millimetre at the edge itself, where the flared facet meets the flat top at an acute angle, which is a ray leaving through the top face and not a thin wall. A 0.6 mm rim fillet built but cost a third of the build and 30k triangles in the browser, and a chamfer would not build on the twisted facets, so the rim is left sharp.
